name: intent-complement-displays-never-surfaces
why: S9 is the intent signal: B has done what A is trying to do. A raising founder (I2) meeting a capital deployer (I1) is a complement, so S9 fires and adds 3 to the DISPLAYED score — but the floor reads S1-S7 only. This pair sits at floor score 5 (S1 + S5), and the S9-inflated display of 8 must not push it over the surfacing line: intent sharpens a real match, it never manufactures one. *** SYNTHETIC, and labelled as such: no member in db/roster.sql carries a measured intent yet, so the two records here are fixture-supplied. Re-ground it when ingest first measures an intent. ***
defends_against: An implementation that adds S9 into the score the floor reads, so a below-floor pair gets surfaced because the intents happen to complement.

properties.name: s9-inflates-the-display-but-not-the-floor
properties.reason: PRD-R-022a.5: the complement class adds S9's 3 to the displayed score, so the host sees 8, not 5.

properties.name: floor-decision-unchanged-by-s9
properties.reason: PRD-R-020: the floor is evaluated on S1-S7 only. This pair's floor score is 5, below 6, so nobody is named no matter how well the intents fit.
